_comment: The total score parity table: the survey runtime (packages/types/surveys/scoring.ts, walked as packages/surveys/src/components/general/survey.tsx walks blocks) and the server's recomputation (score.go) are both run over these cases, by packages/surveys/src/lib/score.parity.test.ts and score_parity_test.go. elements: what one answer earns, null when the element is not scored. surveys: the blocks a response walks and the total it ends with; startAt is the element a link opened the survey at, which only the runtime is told (the server starts at the first block the response holds an answer or a time for). meta is the response meta the reserved values logic conditions read are projected from: only the entries the runtime can read mid-survey, as it projects them.

elements.name: single choice: the picked choice's score
single choice: a choice without a score earns 0
single choice: a label in another language
single choice: free text is the Other choice
single choice: text no choice has, without an Other choice, earns 0
single choice: an empty answer is not scored
single choice: no answer is not scored
single choice: a number is not an answer
multiple choice: each choice counts once
multiple choice: two free texts are the Other choice once
multiple choice: an empty selection is not scored
multiple choice: only strings are read
picture selection: answers are choice ids
picture selection: a label or unknown id earns 0
an element whose choices have no score is not scored
an open text element is not scored

surveys.name: every block answered: each block's points are added, and the total rounded, when it is submitted
a partial response: the blocks not reached yet earn nothing
a jump past a block: the answer the respondent left behind when going back is not counted
a jump to an ending ends the walk
the fallback is taken when no rule holds, and a choice without a score earns 0 and still rounds
a condition on the score reads it with the block's points already added (jump taken)
a condition on the score reads it with the block's points already added (jump not taken)
the score starts from its computed field's default
a computed field that is not a number leaves the declared value as the start
without computed fields the score starts from the declared value
a block without a scored answer leaves the total unrounded
an answer that names no choice earns 0 and rounds the total
a link opened at a later block (startAt) starts the walk there
a condition on a reserved field only the server knows (country) reads as unset, as in the browser
a condition on a reserved field the browser knows (source) reads the response meta
